enhancement.detailedExplanation:
India Code rule: Sections 132–138 address arrangements between primarily liable persons, variance and release affecting surety liability, agreements giving time or forbearance, and the effect of release of one co-surety.

Definition: These provisions identify when a surety is or is not discharged by changes in the principal arrangement or by dealings between creditor, debtor and co-sureties.

Ingredients:
1. Identify the original guarantee and the principal liability.
2. Identify the later agreement, release, time arrangement or variance.
3. Match the change to the precise discharge rule in sections 132–138.
4. For co-sureties, distinguish release of one surety from discharge of the others.
examples: A creditor releases one co-surety; section 138 provides that the release does not, by itself, discharge the other co-sureties.
problemApplication: Apply sections 132–138: identify the guarantee/indemnity relationship, test the statutory condition or discharge rule, address the opposing position, and state the consequence.
keyTakeaways: Sections 132–138 address arrangements between primarily liable persons, variance and release affecting surety liability, agreements giving time or forbearance, and the effect of release of one co-surety.
